issues.legal_issue: A retrospective change making comparative hardship relevant requires orders that omitted that assessment to be set aside and the matter remanded, while leaving an independent finding of bona fide need undisturbed.
material_facts: A landlord sought release of a rented shop for a bona fide need, and the authority found that need established but rejected release after weighing comparative hardship against the landlord.

On appeal, the appellate court did not consider comparative hardship because a Full Bench had held the relevant rule requiring that assessment invalid; it allowed release based on the bona fide need finding.
A later retrospective amendment required comparative hardship to be considered and validated the relevant rules.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the High Court and appellate court orders were set aside, and the matter was remanded for consideration of comparative hardship under the amended law. The finding that the landlord bona fide required the shop was not to be disturbed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21 of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, as retrospectively amended by U.P. Act No. 28 of 1976, required comparative hardship to be considered; the amendment also retrospectively validated Rule 16. The Full Bench decision in Chandra Kumar Shah v. District Judge had treated Rule 16(2) as ultra vires, which explained why the appellate court had omitted the comparison, but the retrospective amendment displaced that basis for the orders. Accordingly, the court remanded for the required comparative-hardship assessment without reopening the distinct finding of bona fide need.

rule.if: release_proceeding_on_appeal and retrospective_hardship_requirement and appellate_decision_omitted_comparison and bona_fide_need_already_found

predicates.release_proceeding_on_appeal: A dispute over release of rented premises was before a court on appeal.
predicates.retrospective_hardship_requirement: A later retrospective legal change required comparative hardship to be considered and validated the rules governing that assessment.
predicates.appellate_decision_omitted_comparison: The appellate court decided the release dispute without weighing the comparative hardship of the landlord and tenant.
predicates.bona_fide_need_already_found: An earlier decision had found that the landlord bona fide required the premises.

issues.definition: When a release appeal was decided without a required comparative-hardship assessment because of a legal position later changed retrospectively, and bona fide need had already been found, the prior orders are set aside and the case is remanded for that assessment without disturbing the need finding.
